title: Briefing for 2026-11-08
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-11-08: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, way more than expected; unemployment rate slips to 4.1%. The October jobs report is out Friday. Here's everything to expect. Here's what the Democratic election rout could mean for the U.S. economy. Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war, warns inflation will near 5%. Voters say the economy drove them to the polls — and blame Trump for their troubles. Analysis: The Democrats have one chance to extract concessions from Trump. Markets will hate it.
global: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack. Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government. No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election. US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme. UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC. With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle.
philippines: Meet Elias Gish, the FEU rookie turning heads in UAAP basketball. Trash to treasure: Made Here turns waste into art at Ibagiw 2026. Why Albayanos turn to Nuestra Señora de Salvación in times of crisis. UP outguns Ateneo in altercation-marred thriller to clinch Final Four anew.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
